summary: This standards-track memo extends SIP so that a call can be refreshed periodically using a re-INVITE or UPDATE request. This lets endpoints and proxies learn whether a session is still alive, so stale state can be cleaned up when a call ended without a proper hangup. It defines new header fields for negotiating the refresh.

eli5.summary: Imagine two friends on a phone call who say hello every so often to check the other is still there. If one stops answering, the call is cleaned up.

questions: how does sip detect dead calls
what is the sip session timer
what does sip 422 session interval too small mean
subtitle: A keepalive for SIP calls, so proxies and phones can tell when a session is really over.

tldr.problem: SIP has no keepalive for the sessions it sets up. If a BYE is never sent or gets lost, call stateful proxies keep state for the call and cannot tell when it no longer applies.
tldr.mechanism: UAs send periodic re-INVITE or UPDATE requests to refresh the session. The interval is negotiated with the new Session-Expires and Min-SE header fields and the 422 response code, and one side is named the refresher.
tldr.outcome: If no refresh arrives before the session expires, the UAs send BYE and proxies can drop their call state. The extension works even when only one UA supports it.

facts.label: Recommended refresh time
facts.value: Once half the session interval has elapsed

facts.label: BYE lead time
facts.value: Minimum of 32 seconds and one third of the interval

today: RFC 4028 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of SIP session timers. It builds on RFC 3261 and uses the UPDATE method from RFC 3311.

sections.title: The Missing Keepalive
sections.content:
The Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) does not define a keepalive mechanism for the sessions it establishes. User agents may learn that a session has timed out by using session-specific mechanisms, such as periodic RTCP packets for audio, but proxies cannot. A call stateful proxy therefore cannot always tell whether a session is still active.

The failure case is simple. A user agent fails to send a BYE, or the BYE is lost to network problems. The proxy keeps state for the call and has no way to learn that the state no longer applies.

RFC 4028 fixes this with a keepalive for SIP sessions. UAs send periodic re-INVITE or UPDATE requests, called session refresh requests. If a refresh does not arrive before the interval passes, the session is considered terminated. The RFC also names a second use: a SIP NAT Application Level Gateway must keep state for the length of a call, and relying on a BYE to remove it is unreliable and opens a potential denial of service attack.
sections.eli5: A call can end without anyone saying goodbye, and the helpers in the middle keep waiting forever. This fix makes the callers check in regularly, so a missed goodbye gets noticed.

sections.title: How the Negotiation Works
sections.content:
A UAC starts by sending an INVITE with a Supported header field carrying the option tag timer. Any proxy on the path may insert or adjust a Session-Expires header field and a Min-SE header field.

Min-SE sets the lower bound for the refresh interval. Its purpose is to stop hostile proxies from setting arbitrarily short intervals that overload their neighbors. Each proxy may raise this bound but may not lower it. Session-Expires sets the upper bound, the time a session-stateful proxy must keep its state. A proxy may lower it, but not below Min-SE.

A proxy that finds the interval too short rejects the request with a 422 response carrying its own Min-SE. The UAC retries with the largest Min-SE it has seen, so the final minimum satisfies every proxy on the path. The UAS then puts the final interval in the 2xx response, along with a refresher parameter saying whether the UAC or the UAS will send the refreshes. Proxies can see the final value on the way back but cannot change it.

The session timer refreshes the session, not the dialog used to set it up, though the two are related. If the session expires, a BYE is sent, which ends the session and, generally, the dialog.
sections.eli5: Everybody along the line says how often they are willing to be pinged, and the longest wait anyone demands wins. Then the two callers agree who will do the pinging.

sections.title: Session-Expires, Min-SE and the 422 Response
sections.content:
Session-Expires carries a delta-time in seconds and is placed only in INVITE or UPDATE requests and in 2xx responses to them. Its absolute minimum is 90 seconds, a bit more than twice what a SIP transaction can take on a timeout. That leaves time to refresh at the halfway point and finish the transaction before expiry. The RECOMMENDED value is 1800 seconds (30 minutes), and entities that insert the header SHOULD NOT choose less. The RFC explains that small intervals cause excess traffic and raise the chance of glare, when both UAs send a re-INVITE or UPDATE at once.

The syntax allows a refresher parameter with the value uac or uas. A compact form, the letter x, is reserved for the header. If the header is absent, the session has no expiration under this mechanism, although other mechanisms, such as local timers, may still apply.

Min-SE carries the minimum session interval in seconds. Its value MUST NOT be less than 90 seconds, and when absent its default is 90 seconds. It MUST NOT be used in responses except 422 responses.

The 422 (Session Interval Too Small) response is generated by a UAS or proxy when a request has a Session-Expires below that server's minimum timer. It MUST contain a Min-SE header field with that minimum.
sections.eli5: There is a shortest allowed wait between check-ins, so nobody can pester you every second. If you ask for too short a wait, you get told the shortest one that is allowed.

sections.title: User Agent Behavior and the Refresher
sections.content:
A UAC that supports the extension MUST include Supported: timer in each request except ACK, even when it does not want a timer. It MAY add a Session-Expires, and if it also sends Min-SE the Session-Expires MUST be at least as large. Using Require or Proxy-Require with timer is NOT RECOMMENDED, because the extension works even when only the UAC supports it. The UAC SHOULD omit the refresher parameter so that negotiation can pick one.

The UAS may reject with a 422, or accept by copying the Session-Expires into its 2xx response. It MAY reduce the value but MUST NOT increase it, and MUST NOT go below Min-SE (or 90 seconds when there is none). The UAS MUST set the refresher value, following the table below. It cannot override a refresher choice the UAC already made. When the response names uac as refresher, the UAS MUST add Require: timer, so the UAC knows to read the header.

Each UA stores the session interval, the session expiration and the identity of the refresher, bound to the dialog. For the refresher, expiration is the last 2xx time plus the interval, and the refresh is RECOMMENDED once half the interval has elapsed. If the UAS does not support the extension and only the UAC asked for a timer, the UAC may still refresh purely for its own benefit, acting as if the response had carried its own value with refresher uac. A 2xx without Session-Expires turns the timer off, even mid-dialog.

In later refreshes the UAC MUST add Min-SE if it has ever received a 422 or a request containing one, using the largest value seen. The Session-Expires SHOULD be the larger of Min-SE and the current interval. The RFC RECOMMENDS UPDATE over re-INVITE when the peer is known to support it, and an UPDATE should not contain an offer. A re-INVITE SHOULD contain one that indicates it has not changed.
sections.eli5: When the call starts, the two callers decide who sends the check-ins. If one of them has never heard of the idea, the other can still do the check-ins alone.

sections.title: Proxy Behavior
sections.content:
Session timers matter mostly to call stateful proxies. A stateful proxy that only tracks transactions MAY follow the rules too, but stateless proxies MUST NOT request session timers, because the processing rules need memory between request and response. A proxy that asks for a timer SHOULD record-route, since otherwise it will not see the refreshes.

On a request, a proxy may insert a Session-Expires or lower an existing one, but never below Min-SE, and it MUST NOT touch the refresher parameter. If the request says timer is supported and the interval is below the proxy's policy, the proxy MAY reply 422 with a Min-SE of at least 90 seconds. If the sender does not support the timer, a 422 would simply fail the call, so the proxy SHOULD instead insert or raise Min-SE and then raise Session-Expires to match. A proxy MUST NOT change Min-SE in a request that advertises timer support, which protects against denial of service attacks.

On the response, if the UAS did not support the extension but the UAC did, the first timer-aware proxy MUST insert the remembered Session-Expires with refresher uac and add Require: timer. Proxies MUST NOT modify a Session-Expires already in a response. A proxy computes expiration as the time it forwards the 2xx plus the interval. When it passes, the proxy MAY free the call state, but unlike a UA it MUST NOT send a BYE.
sections.eli5: The operators in the middle can ask for faster check-ins, but only up to a limit. When the check-ins stop, they quietly tear down their notes about the call without hanging up on anybody.

sections.title: Performing Refreshes and Handling Failure
sections.content:
The side doing the refresh follows the UAC rules. Only a 2xx response to a refresh extends the session expiration. A 422 with a much larger Min-SE does not change the existing expiration, so the UA must still get a refresh through before that time, with the larger interval in its Session-Expires.

If the refresh transaction times out or draws a 408 or 481 response, the UAC sends a BYE. For other failure responses it SHOULD follow the rules for that code, such as retrying a 401 with new credentials, but SHOULD NOT retry continuously on the same error.

The side that is not refreshing SHOULD send a BYE if no refresh arrives before the session expires, slightly before the expiration. The RECOMMENDED lead is the minimum of 32 seconds and one third of the session interval. The RFC notes that firewalls and NAT ALGs may be very unforgiving about SIP traffic after the expiration time, which is why the BYE goes first.
sections.eli5: If your check-in gets no answer, you hang up. If you are the one waiting for check-ins and none come, you hang up a little early, before the doors lock.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The timer lets a proxy or UA force compliant UAs to refresh at a rate it chooses, which opens denial-of-service attacks with significant amplification. The RFC says the attacks come from insiders (legitimate elements on the path) or outsiders (elements that modify messages in transit), and that both cases are handled.

For insiders, a rogue UAC that asks for a tiny interval with refresher uas is stopped by a 422 from the UAS or a proxy, or by Min-SE insertion when no timer support is advertised. A rogue UAS that returns a tiny interval is caught because the UAC copies the current interval into later requests, so proxies see it and reject with a larger Min-SE. A rogue proxy cannot force refreshes unless it stays on the signaling path and sees every request and response.

Outsiders who modify messages in transit can force rapid refreshes, so integrity must be protected hop by hop. SIP S/MIME is not suitable, since the header fields are not end-to-end and proxies edit them. It is RECOMMENDED to send requests with Session-Expires, or Supported with timer, over TLS, and to use the SIPS URI scheme. Proxies that record-route and request a timer SHOULD record-route with a SIPS URI.
sections.eli5: A bad actor could try to make you send check-ins nonstop to wear you out. The rules make sure that someone in the chain says no to a silly request, and the locked line stops outsiders tampering.

sections.title: Example Call Flow
sections.content:
The RFC walks through a call from Alice to Bob via proxies P1 and P2, with both ends supporting the extension. Alice's first INVITE asks for Session-Expires: 50. P1's minimum is 3600, so it answers 422 with Min-SE: 3600.

Alice retries with Session-Expires and Min-SE of 3600. P1 accepts and record-routes, but P2 has a configured minimum of 4000 and rejects with Min-SE 4000. Alice retries once more with 4000 for both, the maximum of the Min-SE values she has seen. Bob copies the value into his 200 OK and adds refresher=uac, so Alice will do the refreshing.

Around 2000 seconds later Alice sends an UPDATE with the same value. Her UA then crashes, and 3968 seconds after the refresh Bob times out and sends a BYE. P1 cannot deliver it and returns a 408 (Request Timeout) to Bob.
sections.eli5: Alice asks for check-ins every 50 seconds. Two operators say that is too often, and the answer grows to 4000. Alice then crashes, and Bob notices the missing check-in and hangs up.

SYNTAX OF THE TWO NEW HEADER FIELDS (RFC 4028)

data.title: Header field syntax
data.code:
Session-Expires  = ("Session-Expires" / "x") HCOLON delta-seconds
                     *(SEMI se-params)
se-params        = refresher-param / generic-param
refresher-param  = "refresher" EQUAL ("uas" / "uac")

Min-SE  =  "Min-SE" HCOLON delta-seconds *(SEMI generic-param)
